subject: Zipline capacity structuring: hybrid reserved commit & burst pool sizing
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@zipline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@zipline.ai>, Kate Morris <kate.morris@zipline.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity / sizing question for Zipline Analytics

Ben — thanks again for the demo last week. As promised, attaching a short sample of our traffic and a described profile so you can recommend a committed capacity approach. High-level:
- Peak request rate: ~420 requests/min (7 rps) for inference endpoints that serve summarized analytics alerts. Peak windows last 20–40 minutes, several times per day.
- Typical prompt + response length: avg 1,250 tokens (prompt ~650, completion ~600).
- P50 latency target: 450ms for single-turn summarization; 95th < 1.2s.
- Concurrency observed: ~110 concurrent in-flight requests at peak; bursts up to ~220 for 5–10 min.
- Model mix: mostly Llama2-70B quantized variants, occasional larger context batches for multistep reasoning.
- Retention/compliance: logs must stay in our VPC; we may go Dedicated for data isolation.

Open Qs for you: what committed pool size (GPUs) do you recommend for a 12-month reserved commit vs a 6-month smaller commit + burst? Also want to understand pricing tiers and any flexibility on ramp credits / discounts for upfront commit. Attached: zipline_workload_samples.csv

Thanks — Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform, Zipline Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@zipline.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@zipline.ai>, Kate Morris <kate.morris@zipline.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity / sizing question for Zipline Analytics

Sanjay — appreciate the profile, that’s very helpful. Quick summary up-front: for the profile you shared we recommend a hybrid reserved + burst model to minimize unit cost while covering short spikes. Below is a conservative sizing and the rationale; I’ve attached the detailed pricing PDF and a small workbook with calculations.

Recommendation (high level)
- Reserved commit: 4x high-memory GPUs (80GB-class equivalents) reserved 24/7 for baseline throughput.
- Burst pool: additional 3x shared GPUs capable of autoscaling into your pool for short spikes (pre-warmed fallbacks available).
- Effective delivered capacity (baseline): supports ~100 concurrent steady requests at <500ms P50 with your token profile. Burst capacity supports sustained spikes to ~240 concurrent for short windows.

Sizing rationale (short):
- Average token processing costs scale roughly with prompt+completion tokens. Using your avg 1,250 tokens, we estimate a single 80GB-class GPU can handle ~350 short requests/min (roughly 6 rps) at the latency targets when requests are well-distributed and KV/prefix caching is effective.
- We sized 4 reserved GPUs to cover steady-state headroom (4 * 350 rpm ~= 1,400 rpm / ~23 rps) allowing baseline SLA coverage and predictable cost.
- The 3 burst GPUs handle surplus during 5–10 min spikes; autoscaling adds capacity quickly but we keep reserved + burst mix to meet cost objectives.

Pricing notes and options
- 12-month committed option: preferred unit price; we can offer a 15% sticker discount off list on the GPU-hours component with a 12-month up-front financial commit.
- 6-month committed option: 8% discount, with 20% higher overage rates for burst use beyond reserved capacity.
- Ramp credits: for a 12-month commit we can offer one month of equivalent credits to help with the initial onboarding tuning (applied as invoice credit).

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf, rationale_pool_sizing.xlsx

Do you want a numeric cost example (USD/mo) for both options? Happy to run the model with the exact token distributions in your CSV and send a worked example.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya@zipline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@zipline.ai>, Kate Morris <kate.morris@zipline.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity / sizing question for Zipline Analytics

Ben — thanks for the clear recommendation. A few clarifying points before we share internally:
1) For the 12-month committed option with 4 reserved + 3 burst, can you provide a per-month USD example (committed rate, expected overage charge per GPU-hour, and how the ramp credit is applied)? We need a simple number we can present to finance.
2) If we commit to 4 reserved GPUs for 12 months but find we need 6 reserved GPUs by month 4, what flexibility/price protection do we get when scaling reserved commitments mid-term?
3) If we instead did 2 reserved + 5 burst, how much worse is unit cost at steady-state vs your 4+3 suggestion?

Also, are there SLA add-ons for guaranteed p95 latency windows? We may need higher SLA on our critical alerting routes.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Shah, VP Product
Zipline Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Zipline pricing leverage / counter strategy

Internal notes (do not forward):
Context: Zipline is pushing hard on cost but needs predictable latency on alerting. They asked for simple finance numbers and mid-term scaling flexibility. They are a mid-stage analytics company with clear growth signals; a modest concession could close a 12-month deal.
Suggested counter positions:
- Offer a worked example: 12-mo commit for 4 GPUs = $XX,XXX/mo (list) -> 15% off = $YY,YYY/mo. Include statement of one-month ramp credit applied as an invoice credit on month 1.
- Mid-term scale: allow an upward adjustment to reserved capacity with price protection (new capacity priced at committed tier for 12-month remaining term if added within first 6 months). For the sales play we typically limit downward reallocations.
- If they ask for deeper discount, trade for either a longer commit (18–24 months) or a stronger minimum monthly invoice guarantee (to reduce churn risk).
- Consider including a p95 SLA add-on for $Z000/mo for their critical alerting route with defined credits for SLA misses.

Can we offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 4% of the first 3 months total instead of the one-month free? That gives them more upfront help while keeping us within pricing guardrails. Thoughts?

— Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@zipline.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@zipline.ai>, Kate Morris <kate.morris@zipline.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zipline capacity structuring: hybrid reserved commit & burst pool sizing

Priya / Sanjay — following our internal review I wanted to put a concise counter-proposal on the table so you have a single worked example to review with finance. We’re happy to iterate but this is what we think balances cost, flexibility, and your SLA needs.

Counter-proposal (final for initial negotiation)
- Commitment: 12-month reserved commit for 4x 80GB-class GPUs (baseline).
- Burst: 3x autoscale burst GPUs attached to the pool; burst usage billed at overage rates but capped in a monthly budget band.
- Commercials (example): list-equivalent $48,000/mo for the 4 reserved GPUs -> committed price after 15% uplift = $40,800/mo. One-month ramp credit applied as invoice credit in month 1 (applied to first invoice).
- Mid-term scaling: within the first 6 months you can add reserved GPUs; added capacity is priced at the committed tier for the remainder of the original term.
- SLA add-on: optional p95 latency SLA for your critical route at $3,500/mo; service credits defined as 5% of monthly committed fee per SLA miss event (capped at 50% per quarter).
- Onboarding credit alternative: we can either apply the one-month free credit or a 4% credit across the first 3 invoices — pick which helps your cashflow more.

Next steps: if this looks reasonable we’ll draft a simple SOW and DocuSign proposal and include the pricing workbook with token-level cost lines. If you want a sensitivity run (2-reserved + 5-burst vs 4+3) I’ll attach a quick snapshot showing unit-cost delta across steady-state and 30-day burst scenarios.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf, rationale_pool_sizing.xlsx
